# Brief for designing a new animal family

Read `docs/FOX_FAMILY.md` first: it is the worked example. A family is data plus art, validated by scripts, with no app code. Same engine and rules as the dinos and foxes.

## Deliverables (only these files; do not edit shared tools)
1. `tools/families/<id>.py`: `FAMILY` (the id), `NAME`, `IS_FREE = False`, `FOOD_LABELS` (names for the engine foods `meat`, `veggie`, `pasta`, in that slot order), `SPECIES` (`id: (name, stage, blurb, recipe)`), `LINE` (species id -> a short line name), `LINE_COLORS` (line name -> muted nostalgic hex for the body colour in Technicolor, plus `'baby'`), `EVO` (parent -> ordered `(child, requirements)`; first match wins; the last entry has no requirements), `BABIES` (two hatchlings).
2. `tools/archetypes_<id>.py`: the pixel bodies. Build with parts so features stay tunable: you may `from archetypes_fox import _G` (a drawing surface with `ell`, `tri(min_h=...)`, `line`, `set`, a size factor `k`, and the transform that stands the animal on row 15). Build every archetype **natively at each stage size** (`by_stage` for stages 1..5, sizes about 0.58, 0.7, 0.86, 1.0, 1.0), never by shrinking the adult, because shrinking erases thin features. Register with `spritegen.register_archetypes({...})` at import time (import `spritegen` from `tools/`). New decorations: `spritegen.EXTRA_HANDLERS['name'] = fn(g, c)` with `c` = dict(hx, hy, hr, ex, ey, b0, b1, f, ox, oy) as in spritegen.draw; name them with your family prefix. Existing decorations are available (leaf, crown, halo, glasses, antenna, scarf, stripes, spots, belly, spikes via back, fur via back, wings, fangs, arms, horn, horns2, crest, noodle, bolt, tails2/3/5, flame via tail, club/curl/fin tails).
3. `docs/families/<id>.md`: a short design doc in the style of FOX_FAMILY.md: concept and tone, the lines, a table of the tree (generate it from the data with a small script and paste), art direction, weak spots, integration notes (anything the app must learn, e.g. new decorations or a new mechanic), open questions.
4. `docs/families/<id>-sheet.png` (16x16) and `docs/families/<id>-sheet-hires.png` (32x32) from `python3 tools/sheet_family.py <id> <out.png> [hi]`.

## Rules
- **Original.** Invent names and designs. Do not use or closely echo any existing game or media creature, character or trademark (no Pokemon, Digimon, Tamagotchi, Zelda, Mario and so on). Generic real-world animals and folklore terms are fine. Keep the tone friendly and all-ages (12+).
- **Species count:** 30 to 40 across five stages: 2 babies, 4 children, 8 to 11 teens, 10 to 13 adults, 5 to 8 ultimates. Every list in `EVO` ends with a guaranteed fallback; the three `lead` branches may serve as the fallback for the baby stage.
- **Species ids must be unique across all families:** prefix every id with `<id>_` (for example `cat_mittens`). Display names are separate and unprefixed.
- **Requirements** use only these keys: `mist_min`, `mist_max` (care mistakes this stage), `train`, `wins`, `smarts` (this stage), `heavy` (bool), `lead` ('meat', 'veggie' or 'pasta' = the food eaten most this stage), `disc` (discipline, cumulative, earned by scolding the pet when it is naughty: +25 each). Use the same magnitudes as the dino and fox trees (`mist_min` 1 to 4, `train` 3, `wins` 2 to 5, `smarts` 12 to 40). Ordinary care (feeding when hungry, cleaning, a few visits a day) must never land on the neglect line; only real neglect does.
- **Every family needs a neglect line** (a stray/ragged/worn line reached by `mist_min`), a way to be reached by each food lead, and branches for training, smarts, battles and heavy.
- **Silhouette first.** The game is a monochrome 16x16 LCD (smoothed to 32x32). Each family must be recognisable in plain ink by 2 or 3 strong features, kept at every size (min feature sizes: ears, tails, wings, fins, horns at least 2 px). Colour is a bonus in Technicolor, not a crutch.
- **Check:** `python3 tools/check_family.py <id>` must print OK (stages step up by one, fallbacks, every species reachable, no branch shadowed). To run it your family module must be importable by name: it is, because `tools/families/` is on the path.
- Work in your OWN worktree (see your prompt), commit often, push only your branch, never push to main. Do not edit `tools/familyset.py`, `tools/spritegen.py`, `tools/archetypes*.py` of other families, or any app code. Look at your sheets with the Read tool and iterate until the animals read well.
